text:
laura: during today's chaos run i reproduced an edge case: gateway preempts upstream worker (OOM) while it's mid-streaming a response. client gets a few tokens, then silence. no trailer, no hint, UI just spins. we should define a graceful-evict contract to avoid opaque failures.

ben: agreed. current behavior is a hard TCP RST -> client treats as error. we talked about resume tokens previously, but i want to explore a lighter-weight approach: emit a synthetic end-of-stream trailer that includes a compact checkpoint (hash+offset) and a typed reason so clients can choose to retry, continue, or surface partial.

nidhi: lightweight trailer is good. what fields do we need? i'm thinking: `x-rw-esc: <evict-code>`, `x-rw-checksum: sha256(<last-n-tokens>)`, `x-rw-offset: <token-count>`, `grpc-status: 8` for recoverable. evict-code enum: {planned, mem-pressure, preempt}.

kevin: caution: not all transports allow trailers (browser fetch + HTTP/1 chunking vs HTTP/2). we should specify fallback: if trailer can't be delivered, gateway must send an in-stream control frame as a prefixed JSON chunk: `{"_rw_evict":{...}}` so clients without trailer support can still see it.

laura: good point. unify into `control frames` concept. model containers should emit a control frame on graceful shutdown. gateway can translate to trailer or inline chunk depending on client capabilities.

ben: tradeoffs: emitting control frames adds a small latency/throughput overhead and requires client lib parsing. but it's backward-compatible if we keep it optional and opt-in per SDK.

nidhi: operational question: who stores the checkpoint? gateway can keep ephemeral resume entries for short TTL (e.g., 45s). for longer or regulated workloads, customers can opt into durable resume where the private control plane persists the checkpoint to tenant storage. we need two modes: ephemeral vs durable.

kevin: add route config: `resume_policy: {mode: ephemeral|durable|none, checkpoint_interval: 128, ttl_seconds: 45}`. default ephemeral. metrics: `edge.evict.control_frame_emitted`, `edge.evict.resume_lookup_hit/miss`.

laura: for ephemeral mode, limit global memory by accounting `mb-seconds` per tenant and enforce admission with a token-bucket. eviction of resume state should respect tenant quota; if quota exhausted, gateway should still emit control frame but mark `x-rw-resume-available: false` so client knows fallback required.

ben: UX-wise, clients should show partial + button "retry and continue". retry flow: client sends `x-rw-resume-request: <evict-id>` header. gateway checks resume store (ephemeral/durable) and routes to model to resume at offset. if resume not available or expired, gateway may route to `best-effort` short-answer model and set `x-rw-resume-fallback: true`.

nidhi: need a clear billing contract: tokens produced before eviction are billed once. resumed tokens are billed normally. if gateway replays tokens server-side to reconstruct state without charging client (for deterministic checkpoints), we must mark those as "replay-overhead" and bill differently. recommend simple rule: resumed tokens are billed to the retrying request; server-side replay to rehydrate state is considered compute overhead billed to tenant by a separate metric `edge.resume.replay_compute_ms`.

kevin: security: evict-id must be unguessable (128 bits) and bound to tenant+route. control frame content must never contain PII or raw prompt. use fingerprints + truncation. document in privacy checklist.

ben: testing: create a new harness `chaos/stream-evict` that injects both soft and hard evicts at random offsets. assert client sees either a control frame or the correct error, and that resume flow reconverges. add fuzz for control-frame JSON injection across HTTP/1/2/3.

laura: also add a canary flag `edge.resume.contract.v1` and gate behavior. rollout plan: enable in canary, collect `edge.evict.resume_hit_rate`, `edge.evict.fallback_rate`. if fallback_rate > 4% for 15m, consider increasing ephemeral TTL or checkpoint frequency.

nidhi: operation runbook snippet: "If resume_hit_rate < 80% and fallback_rate high: 1) check resume-store memory pressure 2) inspect per-tenant mb-second usage 3) consider increasing checkpoint_interval or enabling durable mode for affected tenant."

kevin: small addition: coordinate with SDK teams to add a `ResumeManager` helper that parses control frames/trailers and exposes a unified API: onPartial(resumeMeta) -> UI shows partial + resume button that calls `ResumeManager.resume(evictId)`. ship both Node and Python clients.

ben: ok i'll draft the RFC: sections: contract (control frame + trailer schemas), resume_policy route config, admission & billing, runtime accounting, SDK contract, testplan, privacy checklist, rollout plan.

laura: thanks. can we include an example control frame and sample client flow? copy for RFC: 
INLINE CHUNK (HTTP/1 fallback):
{"_rw_evict": {"evict_id":"e3f2...","offset":4096,"checksum":"ab12...","reason":"mem_pressure","resume_available":true,"ttl":45}}

TRAILER (HTTP/2+):
x-rw-evict-id: e3f2...
x-rw-offset: 4096
x-rw-checksum: ab12...
x-rw-resume-available: true
grpc-status: 8

ben: perfect. i'll open RFC link here when done.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: gateway/edge-proxy v1.44.0 -> canary (eu-west-1) :rocket:

laura: RFC: https://rfc.internal/r/stream-evict-contract (WIP). please review tests & billing section.

kevin: adding reviewers: @sdk-team @billing @security.

nidhi: i'll add the metrics + alert PRs. recommended alert: `EVICT_FALLBACK_RATE > 4% for 15m` and `RESUME_STORE_UTIL > 80% for 10m`.

laura: thanks team. follow-ups: SDK parsing helpers + chaos harness + RFC. low-risk rollout behind feature-flag.
